Mu--Guo 2026 Definition 3 (weight -1 convention)
correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the ternary multiplication [x,y,z]=det(x,y)z_2 e1 from [e1,e2]=e1, so it satisfies Lie triple axioms over every field. For R=[[a,b],[c,d]], independently expanded the eight ordered basis triples to four distinct defect polynomials c(a^2 d-a^2-abc-bc), c^2(ad-a-bc-d), a^2d^2-2a^2d-abcd+abc-bcd, c(ad^2-2ad-bcd+bc-d^2). For c=0 only a^2 d(d-2)=0 remains, giving A (a=0), B (d=0), C (d=2). For c!=0, set Delta=ad-bc; equation two gives Delta=a+d, equation one becomes c Delta=0; hence Delta=a+d=0 and Cayley-Hamilton implies R^2=0. Direct substitution proves every square-zero R solves all defects. The square-zero cone has q^2 points (zero and q^2-1 nonzero rank-one nilpotents); A,B,C each have q^2; A intersect B intersect N is the b-line of q points; A intersect C is a distinct b-line of q points; C intersects B,N trivially in odd characteristic. Inclusion-exclusion yields 4q^2-3q. Only C has nonzero determinant 2a, hence rank-two q(q-1), zero one, rank-one (q-1)(3q+1). For F_{q^m}, substitute q^m in the universal classification, obtaining zeta (1-qT)^3/(1-q^2T)^4. The independent symbolic derivation and exact-integer finite-field checks over F3,F5,F7,F11 checked 17,748 matrices and reproduced rank profiles (1,20,6), (1,64,20), (1,132,42), (1,340,110). The finite checks are corroboration, not a proof over all fields; the exact algebraic case split supplies the unrestricted proof. Characteristic two is explicitly excluded.
residual_risks: The polynomial ideal is analyzed as a reduced set of solutions, not asserted scheme-theoretically reduced or smooth.
Arbitrary extension-field counts follow from the proof, not separate enumeration of F_{q^m}.

evidence: 2026 paper develops cohomology, deformation, extensions and higher structures for arbitrary Reynolds Lie triple systems; its same-object Example 4 is a sufficient affine-plane family for all weights.

Gharbi--Mabrouk--Makhlouf Proposition 3.3 concerns a 2lambda-induced ternary operator from a Reynolds Lie algebra, without implying exhaustiveness of all ternary Reynolds operators.

Two-dimensional pre-Lie Reynolds operators satisfy a bilinear product identity on another algebraic structure; this is not equivalent to the ternary Reynolds identity. For example R=diag(1,2) is ternary Reynolds, but for the pre-Lie product e2·e1=-e1 and all other products zero it fails the bilinear Reynolds identity at (e2,e1).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general literature extends the formalism to larger classes but its reviewed theorems do not impose necessary matrix identities for every Reynolds operator on this fixed triple. The closer same-object result supplies only A; the additional B, C, N, including invertible and c!=0 solutions, require the new polynomial case split. Different pre-Lie or Rota--Baxter identities cannot be substituted without proving a reduction.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge qualified PASS for the complete weight-minus-one Reynolds locus and all-odd-finite-field rank/point-count classification. Mu--Guo (Axioms 15 (2026) 616, Definition 3 and Example 4) uses the same triple system and Reynolds weight convention but explicitly constructs only the first-column-zero plane A, not a necessary-and-sufficient locus. Teng--Jin--Long (Axioms 12 (2023) 934) and Gharbi--Mabrouk--Makhlouf (arXiv:2309.01385) develop broad Reynolds/cohomology theory but no matching all-matrix two-dimensional classification was found in examined portions. Xiao--Teng--Long (Symmetry 16 (2024) 262) contains the same ordinary Reynolds identity in its Hom-Lie triple framework; its example is not a classification. The source proof adds distinct d=0 and d=2 planes and all rank-one square-zero operators, including c != 0, as well as rank counts and the zeta function. These are not consequences of the earlier sufficient plane A alone. Targeted Resultary and published-record/code searches identified only other algebra/operator invariants, no theorem whose hypotheses and conclusion imply this full locus. Direct full-text publisher retrieval for the exact-object 2026 article was HTTP429 and the authorized Oxford source returned vpn_disconnected; consequently absolute priority is not certified.

value.rationale: This is a motivated complete low-dimensional operator classification: the two-dimensional nonabelian Lie triple L is explicitly the first concrete same-object example in Mu--Guo 2026. The published sufficient first-column-zero family A is not exhaustive: the all-field exact solution includes two additional affine planes, the square-zero cone with matrices c!=0, and a genuinely invertible d=2 branch. The full rank stratification over every odd finite field and extension-field zeta function give natural invariants of the resulting operator variety, beyond a one-off numerical table. A future low-dimensional Reynolds/cohomology or deformation computation could use the complete operator-locus stratification as a baseline; this precision is motivated by the original example rather than an arbitrary slice. The point count itself uses elementary inclusion-exclusion but depends on the independently nontrivial full solution-locus classification. No claim about arbitrary Lie triple systems, all weight parameters or characteristic two is made.
residual_risks: This is a first nonabelian example classification rather than a global higher-dimensional structure theorem.
Finite-field zeta follows automatically from the all-field geometry once the classification is established; it is a corollary, not independent novelty.
